resources.string: Send one message to several people you know, as separate SMS
A broadcast sends the same message to each person as a separate SMS from your number. Replies come back to you one to one.
Personal, non-commercial use only: family, friends, your housing society or team.
Send only to people who know you and expect your message.
Spam and unsolicited promotional messages break Dak\'s terms and your operator\'s and telecom regulator\'s rules.
In India, TRAI\'s rules on unsolicited commercial communication (TCCCPR 2018) cover personal numbers too: people can report your number on 1909, and it can be disconnected or blacklisted.
Operators may slow down, block or suspend numbers that send in bulk.
Your normal SMS charges apply for every recipient, and for every part of a long message.
Dak limits a broadcast to %1$d people and %2$d messages a day, and spaces the messages out.
I understand, and will only send to people who expect my messages

Dak is a personal messaging app. Broadcast lists, scheduled sends, forwarding and automations are there to help you talk to people you know.

You must not use Dak to send spam: unsolicited commercial or promotional messages, messages to people who have not agreed to hear from you, or messages to numbers bought, scraped or collected from others.

India: the TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR) forbid unsolicited commercial communication from unregistered senders, including personal numbers. Recipients can report such messages by SMS or call to 1909 or in the DND app. Operators must act on complaints and can warn, restrict, disconnect and blacklist the number.

Everywhere: operators throttle, block or suspend numbers that send in bulk, and many countries have anti-spam laws. Businesses must use a registered bulk-SMS provider, not a personal SIM.

Dak's limits: at most 50 people per broadcast and 100 broadcast messages in any 24 hours, sent in spaced-out batches; no recurring broadcasts; automations can never start a broadcast; premium-rate, short-code and alphanumeric numbers are never broadcast to.

SMS charges from your operator apply to every message you send, including each copy of a broadcast and each part of a long message.

You are responsible for the messages you send. Misuse can lead to your number being disconnected by your operator.

Links and words like offer, sale, discount or click are typical of spam. Unsolicited promotional SMS from a personal number breaks TRAI rules in India and your operator\'s terms: your number can be reported on 1909 and disconnected.
